_: #228 — strings that are user-facing AND must stay one language.
The ledger beside this file counts what is left to translate, and its
target is zero. That target is unreachable while it also counts strings
translating would BREAK, so those are recorded here with the reason, once,
instead of being rediscovered by whoever works the backlog next. An audit
pass already spent two of its findings answering 'leave it'.
An entry is not a way to make a warning go away. Every literal listed here
must still be found in that file by the scanner: an exemption matching
nothing FAILS, so this list cannot outlive the code it excuses. And every
entry needs a `why` somebody can disagree with.
The bar is 'translating this changes behaviour', not 'translating this is

com/loonext/android/core/model/Countries.why: The country list writes into a freeform address column — the string IS the stored value, not a label over it. Translated, the same workspace stores 'United Arab Emirates' for a member reading English and 'Émirats arabes unis' for one reading French, so two contacts at the same address stop matching and any grouping by country splits in half. The list is one language for the same reason a phone number is one format. Only the multi-word names appear here; the scanner reads them as sentences.

Core/Model/Countries.swift.why: Twin of the Android list, and exempt for the same reason: the string is the stored value of a freeform address column rather than a label over it, so translating it makes the same address store differently depending on who typed it.

payments.ts.why: The legacy half of #339's expand-and-contract, and the file says so: this is what the API puts on the wire for clients that predate payoutReadinessKeys, and an old build renders it VERBATIM. Translating it would send French to a build that cannot read a key, and changing a word would change what those builds display. It is deleted, not translated, when those builds are gone — and this exemption fails the moment the function goes, which is the reminder.

contact-relationship.ts.why: Not copy — the EXPECTED-OUTPUT column of CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_CASES, the vectors that hold web, Android and iOS to the same sentence. The module itself is already key-based; these strings are the assertions about it. Translating them would leave three clients agreeing with a French fixture and nothing checking the English they actually render.
